content.title: About
content.content: The Seafood Salad Sandwich is a sandwich that layers a salad made from boiled seafood (shrimp, crab meat, mussels), vegetables, and a light mayo‑based dressing between slices of bread. It is popular in coastal cafés and restaurants, combining the freshness of the sea with a crunchy bun.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first seafood salad recipes appeared in the United States in the 1970s as part of the “seafood salad” trend.
The sandwich is usually served cold, but it can be lightly toasted for extra crunch.
Lemon juice and fresh dill are commonly added for extra aroma.
Variations may include avocado, cucumber, or a splash of soy sauce.
It packs well in cling film for picnics and lunchboxes.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Shrimp and crab provide omega‑3s that support heart health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Seafood offers easily digestible protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many meat sandwiches, this version contains little saturated fat.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Seafood is a good source of B12 and B6, which help maintain nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: zinc and selenium
items.content: Zinc and selenium support immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels, or other shellfish.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared seafood is often salted; people watching their sodium intake should choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth, so keep seafood chilled at all times.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Commercial mayo may contain added sugars and preservatives, which some prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the sandwich in half and enjoy it cold or lightly warmed in a toaster. It pairs well with a simple side salad, fries, or fresh veggie sticks. Optional toppings include mustard or tartar sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. If the seafood salad is prepared separately, keep it chilled to prevent the bread from becoming soggy.
